The test image shows a corn ear with a grayish-green mold covering the kernels, with dried husks pulled back. This is clearly an ear rot disease. Top candidates: Trichoderma_Ear_Rot (green mold), Aspergillus_Ear_Rot (olive-green), Diplodia_Ear_Rot (white mold), Gibberella_Disease (pink mold), Fusarium_Disease (pink/white).

Let me view reference images for these candidates first.

So far I've viewed 5 reference classes. The test image has widespread grayish-green mold on an ear. Trichoderma (blue-green between kernels) and Aspergillus (olive-green powdery) are top candidates. Need to view 11 more different classes to meet the budget of 16.

Now I have 16 views across 16 different classes. Let me make my final assessment.

**Test image analysis:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back
- Widespread dense, powdery/dusty olive-grayish-green mold covering a large section of the ear
- Yellow kernels visible at the unaffected lower portion
- Mold appears as a flat, powdery coating over the kernels

**Comparison:**
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot** (refs 1 & 2): Both show the same dense, powdery olive/grayish-green mold coating large sections of the ear, with yellow kernels exposed at the margins. Texture and color match the test image very closely.
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (ref 1): Shows distinctly teal/blue-green fuzzy mold growing *between* individual kernels — different color and texture pattern than the test image.
- All leaf disease classes (Common Rust, Gray Leaf Spot, Northern Leaf Blight, etc.) are clearly not applicable — different plant part.
- Gibberella, Fusarium, Diplodia: Pink/white molds — don't match.

The test image most closely resembles Aspergillus Ear Rot: dense, powdery olive-green mold coating a section of the ear with yellow kernels exposed at the bottom.
